term: Lists of open-source artificial intelligence software
definition: These lists include projects which release their software under open-source licenses and are related to artificial intelligence projects.
details: These include software libraries, frameworks, platforms, and tools used for machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, computer vision, reinforcement learning, artificial general intelligence, and more.

explainer.lead: These lists catalog open-source AI projects, covering libraries, frameworks, platforms, and tools. They matter because they help practitioners discover reusable software and avoid reinventing components.

tiers.eli5: Think of it as a directory of free, shared toolkits for building AI, so you don't have to make every tool yourself.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers consult these lists to find libraries and frameworks for machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning. A pitfall is that listed projects vary widely in maintenance and quality, so due diligence is still needed.
tiers.paperLevel: No formal definition or formula is given; the lists are compilations of AI-related projects released under open-source licenses, spanning software libraries, frameworks, platforms, and tools.

explainer.example: A developer building a computer vision prototype scans such a list to select an open-source deep learning framework instead of writing vision code from scratch.
